message.content: Before I add a custom 'sticky-note' node type to Eve's canvas, I want a read-only inventory of the @excalidraw/excalidraw element model: the element types, the binding fields, and how version/versionNonce work. Please don't change any code — just read the types and end with a written plan for the custom node.

content.text: Read-only inventory it is. I'll walk the element type declarations, the binding fields on arrows, and the version counters, then write a plan — no edits. Starting with the element union in the package's type declarations.

content.content:
export type ExcalidrawElementType =
  | 'rectangle' | 'ellipse' | 'diamond'
  | 'arrow' | 'line' | 'freedraw'
  | 'text' | 'image' | 'frame' | 'embeddable'

export interface ExcalidrawElementBase {
  id: string
  type: ExcalidrawElementType
  x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number
  angle: number
  strokeColor: string; backgroundColor: string
  version: number          // bumped on every mutation
  versionNonce: number     // random; breaks ties in collaborative merge
  isDeleted: boolean
  boundElements: { id: string; type: 'arrow' | 'text' }[] | null
}

content.text: Good baseline. The element union has rectangle/ellipse/diamond/arrow/line/freedraw/text/image/frame/embeddable, and every element carries version + versionNonce plus a boundElements back-reference. A custom node will need to fit this base shape. Now the binding fields — reading the linear (arrow) element type for startBinding/endBinding.

So bindings live on the arrow as startBinding/endBinding, each a PointBinding of { elementId, focus, gap }. The bound shape doesn't store the binding — it just needs to be a 'bindable' element. I need to check what makes a shape bindable, since the custom node must opt in to be a valid arrow target.

content.content:
node_modules/@excalidraw/excalidraw/types/element/typeChecks.d.ts
12:export declare function isBindableElement(el: ExcalidrawElement): boolean
13:// returns true for rectangle, ellipse, diamond, image, frame, embeddable, text
14:// (NOT arrow/line/freedraw). Custom shapes registered as one of these qualify.

content.text: isBindableElement is true for the container-ish types (rectangle, ellipse, diamond, image, frame, embeddable, text) and false for arrow/line/freedraw. That tells me the sticky-note should present as a bindable container shape so arrows can attach to it. Now how scene mutations and version counters are applied — reading updateScene.

That completes the model picture: updateScene replaces the element array and the reconciler uses version + versionNonce to merge — higher version wins, versionNonce breaks ties. So any custom node MUST bump version and assign a fresh versionNonce on every mutation, or collaborative merges will silently drop its edits. Checking how Eve currently registers/extends element rendering to know where a custom type would plug in.

That settles the approach. Eve already has the right pattern: store custom nodes as a base bindable type (rectangle) carrying customData.kind, and paint the custom look with a React overlay keyed by element.id. So the sticky-note doesn't need a brand-new Excalidraw element type at all — which is good, because the reconciler and binding system only understand the built-in union.

Written plan for the custom sticky-note node (no code changed in this session):
1. Model: represent a sticky-note as a built-in 'rectangle' (bindable, so arrows attach) with customData = { kind: 'sticky-note', text, color }. Do NOT introduce a new ExcalidrawElementType — the reconciler and isBindableElement only know the built-in union.
2. Bindings: because it's a rectangle, arrows bind to it natively via startBinding/endBinding ({ elementId, focus, gap }); no binding code needs to change.
3. Versioning: every mutation to a sticky-note MUST bump element.version and assign a fresh versionNonce, or concurrent edits get dropped by the reconciler (higher version wins, nonce breaks ties).
4. Rendering: keep the existing renderCustomOverlay pattern — Excalidraw draws the rectangle, Eve paints the sticky body via a React layer keyed by element.id.
5. Persistence: customData rides along in updateScene and the autosave scene payload for free, since it's just a field on the element.
Recommendation: ship as customData-on-rectangle, not a new element type. Lower risk, full binding/merge compatibility, and reversible.

message.content: Good — customData on a rectangle is what I hoped. Any risk with the React overlay drifting from the element on fast pans?

content.text: One risk worth recording: the overlay is positioned from element.x/y, so on fast pans/zooms it can lag the canvas by a frame if it reads stale scene coords. The mitigation is to derive the overlay transform from the same appState scroll/zoom Excalidraw uses, in the same render pass — not from a separate effect. That keeps the sticky body locked to the rectangle. No code this session; that's a note for the implementation pass. Inventory complete: element union, binding fields (focus/gap), and version/versionNonce semantics are all captured, and the recommended path is customData-on-rectangle with an overlay.
